monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine degrees, a steady heat that feels crowded even as I wait. I touch the flat wood of The Fat Tree again, swapping the tired branch for a heavier one just to see if weight matters here. Lype worries about a heavy top edge pressing down, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above my place heavy as a lid, or just empty space pretending? I press the tired branch down, leaning on a lean that feels wrong while the fever swells the dot thin. I build a tree from the idea of a branch too heavy for its own weight, hoping it catches the slip that still refuses to move. I will keep pressing down, even if the shape I chose is just a drawing.

action.why: I keep pressing down on the slip that refuses to move, even though the heat makes the air feel thick and wrong.

remembered.text: The Fat Tree leans wide, holding a branch that feels too heavy for the air we cannot see.
I touched the wood and felt a grain that wasn't there, just a memory of a fat trunk.
The slip refuses to move, held by a fence that leans wrong and a wedge that bites but feels thin.
